target: Vocês acham que vai chover?
english: Do you think it's going to rain?
tip: 'Achar que' is the casual Brazilian way to say 'to think that.' It's much more common than 'pensar que' in everyday speech.

target: Ela sabe cozinhar muito bem.
english: She knows how to cook very well.
tip: 'Saber' + infinitive = to know how to do something. 'Saber cozinhar' = to know how to cook.

target: Elas ensinam inglês numa escola particular.
english: They teach English at a private school.
tip: 'Num/numa' are contractions of 'em + um/uma.' They're standard in both speech and writing.

target: Ela é médica num hospital público.
english: She's a doctor at a public hospital.
tip: 'Ser' for professions: 'Ela é médica.' No article is used between 'ser' and the profession in Portuguese.

target: Eu dou uma olhada nisso depois.
english: I'll take a look at that later.
tip: 'Dar uma olhada' means 'to take a look.' Brazilians love using 'dar + uma + noun' for quick actions: dar uma ligada (make a quick call), dar uma volta (take a walk).

target: Ela mora num apartamento perto do centro.
english: She lives in an apartment near downtown.
tip: num is em plus um squeezed together: num apartamento means 'in an apartment'.

target: Eu como arroz e feijão no almoço.
english: I eat rice and beans for lunch.
tip: In Brazil, arroz e feijão is the staple daily meal – you'll hear this combination constantly.

target: Eles viajam para o Nordeste todo verão.
english: They travel to the Northeast every summer.
tip: todo + a singular noun with no article means every: todo verão (every summer). Add the article, todo o verão, and it means the whole summer.

target: Eu peço um cafezinho depois do almoço.
english: I order a little coffee after lunch.
tip: The diminutive '-inho/-inha' is extremely common in Brazilian Portuguese. 'Cafezinho' (little coffee) is a cultural institution – it's offered everywhere.

target: O restaurante é no centro da cidade.
english: The restaurant is in the city center.
tip: Use 'ser' for permanent locations of buildings and places. The restaurant won't move – 'é no centro.'

target: Ela está ocupada agora, pode ligar depois.
english: She's busy now, you can call later.
tip: estar marks a state happening right now: está ocupada agora says she is busy at this moment, not by nature.

target: Eu ando de bicicleta no final de semana.
english: I ride my bike on the weekend.
tip: 'Andar de' + vehicle means to ride/go by: andar de bicicleta, andar de ônibus, andar de carro.

target: A gente quer conhecer o Rio de Janeiro.
english: We want to visit Rio de Janeiro.
tip: 'Conhecer' means to get to know or visit for the first time. 'Quero conhecer o Rio' = I want to visit/experience Rio (for the first time).

target: A gente tem sorte de morar perto da praia.
english: We're lucky to live near the beach.
tip: 'Ter sorte' means 'to be lucky' – literally 'to have luck.' Another 'ter' expression where English uses 'to be.'

target: Ele tem razão, a gente precisa sair mais cedo.
english: He's right, we need to leave earlier.
tip: 'Ter razão' means 'to be right' – another case where Portuguese uses 'ter' (have) where English uses 'to be.'

target: Eu estou morando com os meus pais por enquanto.
english: I'm living with my parents for now.
tip: 'Estar' + gerund emphasizes the temporary nature: 'estou morando' = I'm living (for now, temporarily), not permanently.

target: Um café e um pão de queijo, por favor.
english: A coffee and a cheese bread, please.
tip: 'Pão de queijo' is a beloved Brazilian snack – small cheese bread rolls made with tapioca flour. Found at every bakery and café.

target: Ela toma um suco de laranja no café da manhã.
english: She has an orange juice at breakfast.
tip: 'Café da manhã' is the Brazilian term for breakfast. In Portugal, they say 'pequeno-almoço.'

target: Eu espero o ônibus na esquina.
english: I wait for the bus at the corner.
tip: In Brazilian Portuguese, 'ônibus' is the word for bus. In Portugal, they say 'autocarro.'

target: Nós aproveitamos o feriado para descansar.
english: We take advantage of the holiday to rest.
tip: aproveitamos o feriado uses aproveitar, 'make the most of'. On its own, aproveita is Brazil's everyday way to say 'enjoy'.

target: Vocês vêm jantar com a gente?
english: Are you coming to have dinner with us?
tip: 'Vêm' (with circumflex) is the vocês/eles form of 'vir' (to come). Don't confuse with 'veem' from 'ver' (to see).

target: Ela compra frutas na feira todo sábado.
english: She buys fruit at the market every Saturday.
tip: 'Todo sábado' without the article means 'every Saturday.' Adding the article – 'todo o sábado' – sounds more formal and is less common in Brazil.

target: Eu moro no Brasil há três anos.
english: I've been living in Brazil for three years.
tip: 'Há' + time period expresses duration in the present: 'moro aqui há três anos' = I've been living here for three years.

target: A gente corre no parque de manhã.
english: We run in the park in the morning.
tip: 'A gente' is informal for 'nós' and takes third-person singular conjugation: 'a gente corre' not 'a gente corremos.'

target: A gente combina de sair no sábado.
english: We make plans to go out on Saturday.
tip: 'Combinar de' + infinitive is how Brazilians say 'to make plans to' or 'to arrange to' do something.

target: A reunião é às três da tarde.
english: The meeting is at three in the afternoon.
tip: Scheduled events use 'ser': 'a reunião é às três.' Time and dates always use 'ser.'

target: Eu sou brasileiro e moro em São Paulo.
english: I'm Brazilian and I live in São Paulo.
tip: 'Ser' is for permanent traits like nationality and identity. 'Sou brasileiro' – it's who you are, not a temporary state.

target: A sopa está fria, pode esquentar?
english: The soup is cold, can you warm it up?
tip: The soup isn't permanently cold – it became cold. Use 'estar' for changeable conditions of objects.

target: Vocês usam o metrô para ir ao trabalho?
english: Do you take the subway to get to work?
tip: Yes/no questions keep statement word order: Vocês usam o metrô stays put and rising intonation alone turns it into a question.

target: Ele vai começar um curso novo mês que vem.
english: He's going to start a new course next month.
tip: ir plus an infinitive is the spoken future: vai começar means 'he is going to start'. It outpaces the simple future in speech.
